title: Trombonists Dave Bargeron and Roswell Rudd; trumpeter Lou Soloff
summary: Gil describes trombonist Dave Bargeron's vaudeville background and Lou Soloff. Roswell Rudd's work with Alan Lomax's cantometrics follows.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: How about that. And I have to have a trombone player from the, he's now playing at the Blood, Sweat, and Tears too, he's name is Dave Bargerom (Bargerou?). Now he came from a musical, theatrical family from New England. They had a troupe, I guess the (Bargerou?) family were like a troupe. They played vaudeville a long time ago. Dave was raised in that kind of thing. So it shows in his solos, you know. Sometimes he'll play like a real 1920 style trombone. He heard it playing on records at his parents house. And he's a very interesting player and a lively player. Lou Soloff (I couldn't do without Dave really?). You the First trumpet player. He's with Blood Sweat and Tears too. But he flew down to play that concert with me that afternoon and flew right back to Rochester that evening again to play the evening jazz. He had to like it a lot to do that.

Then (Roswell Rudd ?) Red took Dave Bargerou's (Bargerou's?) place on trombone that day. And (Roswell was a very talented composer and player. And he works for (Al Lomax. ( ?) he's had several guys, he was around one time, /but before him ( ?). He has, when he thought of

a word, which is a great thing to think of when you are getting a grant you know, it's called cantometrics. Which means measuring a song, right? He's measuring all the world folk music. All the world folk music for its sociological implications and all that.
I've seen him demonstrate that. His great charts, and yes.................... with (LAUGHTER). And he's done this / ?) African music.
Last time he demonstrated with African music.

He put out a couple of albums. He produced, I should say, two African albums for Columbia which I would recommend to anybody. They were called, one's called British East Africa, and one's called French West Africa, music. And actually they are only samples, what you call a sample. And they are a bit frustrating because they don't last long enough. Each one, but he tries to get some interesting thing, but xxxx they're not, they are nice albums.
